predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: the Judean countryside round Modein, from which Mattathias and his five sons 'fled to the nearby mountains'

successors.name: Judea
successors.text: Judea round Jerusalem: Cliopatria's Judea shape of -144, whose independence Demetrius II recognised in 142

ledger.x: 167 BCE: the Maccabees rebel against the Seleucids.

167 BCE: the first battle, the Ascent of Lebonah, is listed under 167 BCE and Beth Horon in 166 ('the Battle of Beth Horon in 166 BCE'); 'Much of the combat in the revolt took place in hilly and mountainous terrain'.
160 BCE: Judas dies at Elasa and Jerusalem is lost.
152 BCE: Jonathan takes the high priesthood in Jerusalem.
152 BCE: the rebels reach autonomy under the Seleucids.
145 BCE: Ekron and three toparchies come to Jonathan.
142 BCE: the fighting ends with the tax exemption; the page's war runs on in skirmishes 'until 134 BCE'.
142 BCE: the rebel state becomes independent Judea. the Hasmoneans gained independence, with Simon's appointment as High Priest around 141 BCE; Jonathan died in 143.

wars.name: Maccabean Revolt
wars.outcome: The Maccabees held the Judean hills, took Jerusalem in 164, lost it after Elasa in 160, reached informal autonomy in 152 and independence in 142; 'conflict between the Maccabees, Hellenized Jews, and the Seleucids continued until 134 BCE'.

wars.name: Jonathan's war against Diodotus Tryphon
wars.outcome: 'In 143 BCE, Diodotus Tryphon went with an army to Judea and invited Jonathan to Scythopolis'; he executed Jonathan at Baskama east of the Jordan.

certainty.note: The rebels' land is a guerrilla and then autonomous hill country: no page gives a boundary; the shape is Cliopatria's Judea of -144.
